html:
The German protectorate over the coast of Togo, declared after the explorer Gustav Nachtigal signed a treaty with a chief at Togoville on 5 July 1884, during the Scramble for Africa.

Germany pushed inland and called it a model colony, as it paid for itself through palm oil, cotton and cocoa. It built a wharf at Lome, three railways from the coast, and a powerful radio station at Kamina, using forced labour and hard taxes. German rule ended in the Togoland campaign of 1914, and the land was split between Britain and France. The French part became Togo; the British part joined Ghana. See also the German Empire.
